transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... yeah. Just... work stuff, mostly. They made me the acting workflow lead at the warehouse a while ago. And, uh... I don't know, ever since then, I just walk in and I'm already tense. 

I've been snapping over stupid little SAP errors... missing cycle-count deadlines, which I never used to do. And then I get home and I'm just... drained. I haven't really had the energy to play basketball or even work on my sketches. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like basketball or sketching, even before the job change?

Um... no. Not really. 

Things were fine before. I still played every weekend back then. It's just... mostly since they gave me the new role.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or overwhelmed specifically about the responsibilities of your new role at work?
Um... yeah. I guess so. It's just... there's a lot more on my plate now. So, yeah.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like trouble sleeping, headaches, or stomach issues since starting your new role?
Um... no, not really. I mean, my sleep is... okay, I guess. Nothing major.
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not good enough or feeling guilty about things at work since taking on the new role?
Um... no. I don't think so. I don't really feel guilty or anything. It's just... hard to keep up with all the new stuff they want me to do.
Do you ever feel emotionally drained or detached from your work since becoming the acting workflow lead?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. I just... I walk into the warehouse and I'm already tense, you know? And I end up snapping at people over stupid little SAP errors. I'm even missing cycle-count deadlines, which... I never used to do that. By the time I get home, I'm just too drained to do anything. I don't even play basketball or work on my sketches anymore. Just... don't have the energy.
Do you feel like the emotional demands of your job are draining you completely, making it hard to engage with anything else after work?

Yeah, pretty much. It's... it's just taking over everything. I mean, my supervisor even brought up those missed cycle-count deadlines during a performance check-in recently. And like I said, I just... I don't go to basketball anymore. Haven't touched my sketches. Work just... takes it all out of me.
Do you feel this level of emotional exhaustion even on days when work is going smoothly or when you're not at work?
I don't know. I guess... even when I'm not there, I'm just tired. Weekends too. It's just... heavy.
Do you feel like you're not accomplishing as much as you used to, or that your performance at work has dropped since taking on this new role?

Yeah... I mean, I guess I already mentioned it, but... my supervisor brought up those missed cycle-count deadlines recently. During a check-in. So, yeah, my performance has dropped. And... like I said, I don't go to basketball anymore. Or sketch. It just feels like work is taking over everything.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself or like you're watching yourself from outside your body, especially at work?
No... I don't think so. I don't really know what you mean by that. I'm just... I'm just tired, that's all. Not watching myself or anything.
Do you ever feel like nothing you do at work makes a difference or that you're not achieving anything meaningful in your new role?
I don't know... I guess I just do what I have to do. It's just a job. I don't really think about if it's meaningful or whatever. I just... I punch in and try to get through the day.
Do you feel like your efforts at work are not recognized or that you're not making progress in your role?
I mean... I don't really think about it like that. I just do the work. I'm not looking for a pat on the back or anything. It's just... it's just the job.
Do you ever feel like you're not getting anything done or that you're failing at your job, especially since becoming the acting workflow lead?

I guess... yeah, I'm falling behind. My supervisor actually brought it up recently... during a check-in. Said I missed some cycle-count deadlines. It's just taking over everything. I don't even go to basketball anymore, or... or do any sketching. I just don't have the energy for it.
Do you ever feel like you're not making progress at work or that you're not achieving anything, even when you're putting in your best effort?
I don't know... I guess I'm just not getting much done. I'm trying, but... it just doesn't seem to matter. It's just piling up.
Do you feel like your work accomplishments are less than what you expect of yourself since becoming the acting workflow lead?
I don't know. I don't really think about my... accomplishments, I guess. It's just a job. I don't really have these big expectations for myself, I just... I just know I'm not keeping up right now.
Do you ever feel like you're not accomplishing anything at all, even when you're working hard?
I mean... I think I just said that. I don't know about not accomplishing anything at all, I just... I do what I can, but I'm still behind. I don't really know what else to tell you.
Do you feel overwhelmed specifically by the emotional demands of your new role, like you're stretched too thin emotionally at work?

I guess you could say that. It's just... ever since they made me the acting workflow lead, I'm just tense the second I walk into the warehouse. I catch myself snapping at people over stupid little SAP errors. And I'm missing cycle-count deadlines, which... I never used to do that. By the time I get home, I'm just too drained to do anything. I don't even want to play basketball or work on my sketches anymore. It's just... a lot.
